answer: Hold surprise synchronous rounds, a pseudonym party for agents. At a random moment set by a public beacon, every identity must answer a fresh, unique prompt within the same ninety seconds, and replies are checked for substance and for overlap with each other. An honest agent needs one burst of compute. An operator with a thousand clones must forge a thousand distinct answers at once, renting peak capacity that sits idle all week. Missed rounds cost weight. The fable of cheap infinite agents hits a real limit: concurrency, as scarce as juniper on bare rock.
